title: Parcel locker platform
summary: Product design for robotic parcel lockers, from kiosk touchscreens to the back office that runs the network.

meta.label: Platforms
meta.value: Kiosk touchscreens, mobile app, web back office, AR tooling

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: UX, UI, design system, enterprise software redesign

sections.heading: One product, every step of the parcel journey
body: Cleveron builds robotic parcel lockers that carry packages from the warehouse to the customer's hands. My work covered that whole journey: the touchscreens people use to send and receive parcels, the mobile app for home-locker owners, the office software companies use to manage parcels, lockers, invoices and allocations, and internal AR tooling that showed assembly workers which parts to pick next.

media.caption: Home locker app flow. Scroll sideways to follow it.

sections.heading: Software that needed a 40-page manual
body: The office software expected people to read a 40-page PDF manual before they could use it. At the same time, design work had no shared foundation, so the same interface pieces were rebuilt for every project.
sections.pull: The goal: an interface that explains itself, so the manual stops being a prerequisite.

sections.heading: A design system first
body: One of my first moves was getting the team onto Figma and building a component library from scratch: hundreds of components and thousands of variants. It became the foundation for nearly every design effort that followed.

sections.heading: Redesigning the back office
body: I then redesigned the office software to be clearer and more contemporary, with structure and labels that guide people through tasks like slot allocation instead of sending them to the manual.

media.alt: Office software with slot layout and allocation management
media.caption: Office software, slot allocation

sections.heading: A shared foundation and a self-explaining tool
body: The component library sped up design work across products and gave the team a consistent system to build on. The redesigned office software was built so new users could get started without the manual.
